Summer break is meant for fun and time with family and friends, but students don't really notice that they are losing the skills and knowledge they've collected. They really only care about having fun, not learning. Students always look forward to summer break, but tend to slowly lose some of the knowledge that they've retained throughout the school year. This results in not being prepared for the up-and-coming school year. Students come in confused and unprepared causing them to fall behind. Imagine coming to school on the very first day and having a hard time remembering certain topics. Your ability to understand your favorite subject has slowly slipped away, and the teacher is moving on to more complicated topics. This sets you back and makes it harder for you to understand the new topics being taught. If most or all of the class is confused and having a hard time, some teachers are forced to push back lessons in order to ensure that everyone is caught up, while others may just move on creating further confusion. It puts teachers at an ultimatum; Should he/she risk the completion of their curriculum for the new year to help the students who couldn't retain the previous knowledge, or move on knowing that these people may not pass their class? Teachers have found a way to solve this annual issue without having to reintroduce a topic to the class. They have created summer projects. These projects usually have something to do with the new curriculum for the new school year. Whether it's a reading assignment, essay, or even a vocabulary assignment, it is all meant to prepare the students and get them thinking early. A discussion was set in motion on the topic of: Should summer projects be student designed or teacher designed? Summer projects should be teacher designed because teachers know what skills all of their students need in their classroom in order to succeed and carry on with the rest of the year without any setbacks or complications.

When designing project assignments, teachers make sure that this project will develop a better understanding of a topic in the student's mind. They base it off of what skills these students need to acquire and improve their class's ability to comprehend the topic. For example, a student wouldn't know how to create a project for algebra 2 if they had just completed geometry and have no background knowledge of algebra 2. They would need a teacher's guidance and detailed directions to complete this project. This also creates a level of understanding for the student coming into the class. During the summer, students lose thought of these topics, but if teachers created projects for them during this time, they would come in fully prepared. Everyone would have an equal level of understanding because they all are prepared for the same thing. Equal opportunity is very important in a classroom because every student needs to feel like they can comprehend what they are learning in order to succeed. If students go out on their own and design their own project, they may not feel pushed to try their hardest. A teacher creates equal opportunity by creating the same guidelines for all the students. Teachers also have experience with students in the past and know what topic to hit the hardest based on experiences. They will design these projects to push the class to their highest potential and make sure that each student is taken care of.

Student designed projects wouldn't be a smart idea because kids tend to do the bare minimum. If students design their own project, they won't know what topics to understand or why they are studying a certain topic. This leads to an unequal understanding of a topic which doesn't help students in the future. They might just do a little assignment that doesn't require much work or effort that doesn't challenge them just to enjoy their summer a little more. Yes, some students work hard, but they all come in not knowing what exactly this new year is going to bring. Students should have the right to think on their own and create new ideas, but this should be further down the school year once the teacher is certain they understand what they are learning. For example, in my English class, our teacher made us all read and annotate the same book. Once we came to class she gave us a vague writing prompt asking what the argument was in the story. Because we have all read he books and annotated it how she wanted, we were all able to write this essay and understand it. Some may argue that a student needs the freedom to learn on their own, but also need to consider the fact that not every student wants to try as hard or even challenge themselves. This is why students need a guide to show them the way in order to create a better understanding. It's a basic understanding that in order to succeed and be independent, one needs to have grasped some knowledge and relied on a teacher to have given the knowledge. This is why there are teachers in the world. They are here to be there for someone and be there as their guide because they know what is best for them in education.

To conclude this argument, teacher based summer projects are the best way to insure a student's ability to succeed in their class. It takes out the factor of inequality and allows the student to hold onto previous and future knowledge. This helps them understand what they are learning in class and reduces the risk of getting left behind. Teachers are here to guide their students to success and cannot do so if their students are lost and getting left behind. If it were student designed, they would be least likely to push themselves to their greatest potential. They also wouldn't know what to study. These points should be considered in the topic discussing whether teacher designed or student designed is the best possible option for a student.

The legalization of marijuana is a highly debated topic among politicians, health professionals, and the general public. While some argue that it should be legalized for medicinal and recreational purposes, others believe it should remain illegal due to its potential harms. In this essay, I will argue against the legalization of marijuana, highlighting the adverse effects it has on society, health, and youth.

Firstly, legalizing marijuana would send a wrong message to the youth, implying that drug use is acceptable and harmless. As a result, there would be an increase in drug use among young people, leading to negative consequences such as impaired cognitive development, decreased motivation, and increased risk of addiction. According to the National Institute on Drug Abuse, marijuana use among high school students has already increased significantly over the past decade, and legalization would only exacerbate this problem.

Secondly, marijuana use has been linked to a range of health problems, including respiratory issues, increased heart rate, and psychological disorders such as depression and anxiety. Long-term use of marijuana can also lead to cognitive impairment, memory loss, and decreased IQ. For example, a study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association found that heavy marijuana users experienced a significant decrease in IQ between the ages of 18 and 32. These health risks are particularly concerning for young people, who may not be aware of the potential harms associated with marijuana use.

Thirdly, legalizing marijuana would lead to an increase in drug-related crime and accidents. While some argue that legalization would reduce crime by eliminating the need for a black market, history has shown that this is not the case. In Colorado, for example, where marijuana is legal, there has been an increase in drug-related arrests, particularly for edible marijuana products. Additionally, the legalization of marijuana would likely lead to an increase in drugged driving, which would pose a significant threat to road safety.

Finally, legalizing marijuana would undermine the efforts to combat drug addiction and substance abuse. As a society, we have worked hard to reduce drug use and promote healthy lifestyles, and legalizing marijuana would send a contradictory message. It is important to maintain a strong stance against drug use and to provide support for those struggling with addiction, rather than sending a message that drug use is acceptable and harmless.

In conclusion, the legalization of marijuana is not a solution to societal problems, but rather a recipe for disaster. It would send a wrong message to the youth, pose health risks, increase drug-related crime and accidents, and undermine efforts to combat drug addiction. Therefore, I strongly argue against the legalization of marijuana and urge policymakers to consider the long-term consequences of such a decision.

I believe students can benefit from the option to attend classes from home through distance learning. Here are some reasons why:

Firstly, distance learning provides flexibility that accommodates different student needs and schedules. Some students have health issues or disabilities that make attending a physical classroom difficult. Distance learning allows these students equal access to their education. It can also help students who have job or family responsibilities outside of school by reducing travel time and allowing them to learn on their own schedule. 

Secondly, distance learning equips students with important online learning skills that are valuable in today's digital world. By engaging with classes virtually, students practice navigating online platforms, participating in video chats, submitting assignments digitally, and managing their time for self-paced work. These technical and self-motivation skills will serve students well whether they pursue further education or enter the workforce. 

Thirdly, distance learning has the potential to improve focus and engagement for certain learners. By removing classroom distractions, students who work well independently may find it easier to concentrate at home. Distance learning also offers multimedia resources like recorded lessons, interactive assignments, and educational games that can make the learning experience more stimulating for digital natives. Teachers too can use analytics to track participation and gauge understanding in new ways.

Of course, there are also some potential disadvantages like lack of face-to-face interaction and guidance from instructors. But for students seeking or requiring flexibility, distance learning provides accommodation that supports education access and builds useful skills for the modern world. Overall, the benefits of optional distance learning seem to outweigh the drawbacks for many students.

The introduction of driverless cars into the future of transportation marks a significant milestone in the evolution of automobiles. Although these autonomous machines are still being tested and perfected, their advantages in terms of safety, convenience, and efficiency make them a promising innovation. In this essay, I will discuss the potential benefits driverless cars offer to various aspects of modern life, while addressing both the challenges associated with implementing this technology and the possible ways to overcome these hurdles. 

First, let's explore the significant advantages driverless cars present regarding road safety. Human error is widely acknowledged as a leading cause of automobile accidents – a factor that driverless cars are well-equipped to overcome. By eliminating distractions caused by drunk, tired, or otherwise inattentive drivers, autonomous vehicles could significantly reduce the number of accidents resulting in death and injury on public roads. Additionally, as they rely on advanced sensor systems to detect and respond to road situations in real-time, autonomous vehicles are likely to have superior reaction times, enhancing their overall safety.

Another notable benefit of driverless cars is the increased convenience they hold for travelers. The time spent behind the wheel can be utilized for other activities, as commuters can work, read, or relax during their journey. This added efficiency could lead to a reorganization of time usage around transportation, potentially boosting productivity levels and enabling people to utilize personal transportation for new purposes.

In addition, driverless cars may have a tremendous positive impact on the environment. Autonomous vehicles have enormous potential for improving fuel efficiency across the board. For instance, fleet vehicles can be optimized to take the most fuel-efficient routes and drive at the most effective speeds, minimizing unnecessary gas consumption. This could lead to significant reductions in CO2 emissions, improving air quality for both humans and wildlife. 

However, it is crucial to recognize and address the potential challenges associated with driverless car implementation. One notable concern is the lack of proper infrastructure or regulations to govern driverless vehicles. The absence of clear legal guidelines and standards for their operations may lead to unintended consequences or confusion among users, and increase the likelihood of crashes.

Another substantial hurdle to overcome is the cost of implementing and maintaining such sophisticated technologies. While driverless cars may offer long-term cost savings through reduced liability on insurance companies and potential fuel efficiencies, the initial investments required for their development and manufacturing pose a significant financial burden. 

Furthermore, an important concern is the ethical dilemmas that may arise during emergencies involving autonomous vehicles, such as making split-second decisions while attempting to avoid accidents or prioritizing passenger safety versus the safety of pedestrians. Programming these systems with unbiased, ethical decision-making principles will be a significant challenge and an essential part of their successful implementation.

To ensure the development of safe and successful driverless cars, it is vital for stakeholders from industry, academia, and government to collaborate and discuss potential roadblocks. Open discussion about safety protocols, infrastructure planning, and technology development will be essential to address the ethical considerations and privacy concerns surrounding driverless transportation. Moreover, as the technology continues to advance, it is imperative to monitor how it impacts various areas of our society, ensuring these innovations are not only valuable to our future but are also responsible to the ever-changing global communities we live in.

In conclusion, driverless cars hold the promise to revolutionize transportation, increasing road safety, adding convenience, and potentially improving environmental conditions. However, it is equally important to consider the challenges that stem from the complexity of autonomous vehicles and prepare for their implementation in a responsible, ethical way. Ultimately, the introduction of driverless cars to the world marks an exciting chapter in our human endeavors and brings forward the responsibility for us to harness new technologies for the betterment of modern society.

I disagree with the principal's decision to mandate participation in extracurricular activities for all students. While extracurriculars can provide valuable experiences, they should remain optional rather than compulsory. Forcing involvement removes student autonomy and ignores differing priorities and circumstances. 

Not all students have the time or interest to commit to extracurricular activities. Some may have jobs or family responsibilities outside of school that prevent them from taking on additional commitments. Others may prefer focusing their energy on academic studies, so they can dedicate time to homework, tutoring or test prep. Extracurriculars are not effective if a student is participating solely due to obligation rather than personal motivation. Forced participation will not lead to passion or skill development in the way that voluntary involvement could.

Making extracurricular activities compulsory also fails to accommodate diverse student needs and talents. While some excel in sports, others may have greater artistic or technical strengths. By limiting options to participation alone, rather than achievement, the policy does not allow students to cultivate their unique skills and interests. Not every student's talents and passions align with standard extracurricular offerings. The options should remain open-ended, so individuals can choose activities matching their specific abilities and goals. 

Finally, mandating extracurriculars risks overburdening students who already have difficulty balancing school work with other obligations. The additional time commitments could negatively impact academic performance or mental health for students who feel stressed by packed schedules. Exceptions should be made on a case-by-case basis, so educators can work with families to design participation plans appropriate for each student's circumstances.

In conclusion, while extracurricular involvement offers benefits, high school students will derive the most value from activities they choose to pursue voluntarily based on their own motivation and interests. Forcing uniform participation policies ignores differences in priorities, talents and personal responsibilities. Exceptions and flexibility are needed to support each student's unique needs and maximize their potential for success. Overall student development is best achieved through optional rather than compulsory extracurricular programs.

Are cars beginning to go out of fashion? Over the last few years, fewer and fewer people are getting their driver's license, and fewer people are buying cars. That's because walking or taking public transportation where you need to go can be more beneficial than driving. Using alternative transportation decreases stress, lowers air pollution, and eliminates the cost of owning a car. These reasons are causing people to eliminate personal vehicles out of their lives.

To begin, using alternative transportation can lower stress. Millions of people around the world face the same problem every morning and afternoon: traffic. Traffic jams cause people to be late for work, causing their stress levels to go up. Stress can lead people into depression or become tense. Eliminating a car from someone's life can allow them to be happy. Instead of driving, many people are starting to walk to work, or take a public bus to where they need to go. If more people begin to stop driving, the roads will be less jammed, which will lower road congestion, leading to less stress. Getting rid of your car can be a key element to eliminating stress.

Second, walking or taking a bus lowers air pollution. In France, air pollution was so bad, the government set an one day ban on driving motor vehicles. Instead, residents could take public busses free of charge, or walk. Anyone who decided to drive their vehicle on the day they were banned, faced a $31 fine. Another city in Colombia also started a similar campaign. Government officials in Bogotá, Colombia set a one-day ban in the city called "the Day Without Cars". The turnout was large, people rode busses, rode bikes, or walked to wherever they needed to go. This eliminated traffic jams, and lowered air pollution. Violates of the ban had to pay a $25 fine. Other countries surely will soon do the same thing.

Lastly, the cost to own a car is far too expensive. Buying a car leads to many problems. The cost of paying off your car after you buy it can overwhelm many people. Having to pay hundreds of dollars every month to repair your car or pay for gas can lead you into debt. Many individuals have become homeless because they can't afford to pay for the things they need, such as a car. Without a car, you save thousands of dollars you can use to pay off other things you might owe.

To conclude, using alternative transportation instead of a car can be very beneficial. It lowers stress, eliminates air pollution, and eliminates the expenses of a car. More and more people are beginning to outlaw cars from their lives, and it is helping the world as well as themselves.

“Have you ever heard about the face on Mars?” My friend asked me during lunch today. “It's proof that aliens exist,” she said confidently.

Being an 8th grader who loves astronomy, I had indeed read about it, only to be told by NASA it was all just a geological landform.

I had read ‘Unmasking the Face on Mars,' written in response to the 25th anniversary of the discovery. It discussed how Viking 1 spacecraft in 1976, photographed the “Face” – a natural rock formation resembling a face - in the Cydonia region of Mars. Initially believed to be of alien origin, the image became widely popular, fueling various sci-fi films and conspiracy theories.

However, after years of speculations and conspiracy, NASA was finally given the opportunity to take better images of the “Face,” and the result was shocking! The images showed that the face in Cydonia was merely a mesa-like geological formation, much like those we have here on Earth.

To begin with, the article states that the “Face” was formed by natural rock erosion over many thousands of years; it was nothing more than an illusion. Secondly, it mentions that the mesa-like formation was similar to other mesas in the Cydonia region, further suggesting that the “Face” wasn't something unusual, as initially perceived.

Moreover, the Mars Global Surveyor's images of the Face in 1998, using laser altimetry, confirmed the geological origin of the formation. In simple terms, the “Face” was created due to wind and water activity and wasn't the result of some extraterrestrial activity.

Furthermore, Cydonia's geological location near the ancient Martian ocean boundary raises questions about the red planet’s past rather than the present, which further proves the point. The formation is a natural geological land-form, much like the various buttes and mesas found all over the earth's landscape; it has nothing to do with aliens.

In conclusion, while the Face on Mars might make for an interesting sci-fi story, it's not something to be taken seriously in reality. NASA, with the assistance of various advanced technologies like laser altimetry and satellite images has proven the "Face'' as nothing more than an unusual-looking rock formation due to natural forces on Mars. The idea of aliens existing might remain a mystery for now, but we shouldn’t confuse a geological formation for something extraterrestrial.
